issues.main_description_html:
Previous Route : {{base_url}}/cronjob/broadcast-post

Broadcast:

  • Broadcast Single Sender
  • Broadcast Double Sender
  • Broadcast Any Sender

Type Broadcast:

  • Website
  • Mobile

Route: {{base_url}}/cronjob/broadcast-post

  • Prevent Broadcast Post Subscribe if Status Post Visibility is Private or Unlisted with error message "Notification not allowed for unlisted and private visibility" for Owner Post

Docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XEa0p1yuB7cRH9z42pQluFYV_EtkEqxpzV0yb8UROBQ/edit?tab=t.0

QA Summary - 28 July 2026

Result: Bug found. Dev notification staging correctly rejects private and unlisted posts, but the Dev broadcast cronjob crashes with HTTP 500 while processing the staged public-post queue.

Real API Evidence

Scenario Endpoint Test data / payload Response Result
Missing authentication POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/notification/add-post Public post payload without Authorization 401 - Unauthorized Pass
Required input Same endpoint {} 400 - Required input body Pass
Private post guard Same endpoint Tester-owned private post c9ac5b402b5-2026072408435400 403 - Notification not allowed for unlisted and private visibility Pass
Unlisted post guard Same endpoint Tester-owned unlisted post fc96747121e-2026072408432200 403 - Notification not allowed for unlisted and private visibility Pass
Public post staging Same endpoint Tester-owned public post gad5657ea34-2026050708314600, test: true 200 - Success Send notification Pass
Broadcast cronjob GET https://app2-dev.panorra.com/cronjob/broadcast-post Processes staged Dev queue 500 - interface conversion: interface {} is map[string]interface {}, not string Bug

Test data: account testergothru@gmail.com; Dev username devaccount; public post gad5657ea34-2026050708314600; private post c9ac5b402b5-2026072408435400; unlisted post fc96747121e-2026072408432200.

No new post was created or published for this run. The approved existing tester-owned posts were used, so there is no created post to delete.

Confirmed Coding Bug

GET /cronjob/broadcast-post returns HTTP 500 after a successful public notification-staging request. The live error indicates an unsafe type assertion: a value already decoded as map[string]interface{} is handled as string. In Broadcast.go, the cronjob decodes send_data into a map and then attempts to cast panorama_quality or location_post as string before decoding again. The response error is developer-actionable and prevents broadcast delivery.

Copyable Requests and Responses

Authentication:

POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/auth?ec=false
Content-Type: application/json
ec: false
{
  "email_username": "testergothru@gmail.com",
  "password": "[REDACTED]",
  "ec": "false",
  "v": 1
}

Public notification staging:

POST https://app2-dev.panorra.com/notification/add-post
Authorization: <COPY_TOKEN_FROM_LOGIN_RESPONSE>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "action": "addPost",
  "body": "[name] added a new post",
  "sid": "gad5657ea34-2026050708314600",
  "test": true
}
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Success Send notification"
  }
}

Private or unlisted visibility check: replace sid with c9ac5b402b5-2026072408435400 or fc96747121e-2026072408432200.

{
  "statusCode": 403,
  "data": {
    "valid": false,
    "status": "Forbidden",
    "errors": {
      "message": "Notification not allowed for unlisted and private visibility"
    }
  }
}

Cronjob bug reproduction:

GET https://app2-dev.panorra.com/cronjob/broadcast-post

Actual response:

HTTP 500
interface conversion: interface {} is map[string]interface {}, not string

Code Review Summary

Area Evidence Result
Route GET /cronjob/broadcast-post calls CronjobAction.Broadcast. Route reachable; live 500 reproduced
Notification staging POST /notification/add-post checks post ownership and published status. Pass
Visibility guard AddPostSubscribe rejects any visibility other than public. Pass; private and unlisted live 403 confirmed
Queue payload AddPostSubscribe serializes post payload fields including JSON fields. Public staging returned 200
Cronjob JSON handling Broadcast unmarshals send_data, then treats JSON fields as strings. Fail; unsafe assertion causes live HTTP 500
Delivery cleanup Containers are deleted only after successful processing. Blocked by crash; not claimed as verified

Coverage Matrix

Method Coverage Outcome
Black-box Real Dev auth, required-input, private/unlisted, public staging, and cronjob calls. Cronjob failed with 500
Gray-box Staged payload behavior was matched to its queue-processing endpoint. Failure occurs at the staging-to-cronjob boundary
White-box Route, staging guard, queue serialization, and cronjob decoding paths were reviewed. Type-handling defect aligns with live error

Confusion Matrix

Actual scenario Expected classification Observed classification Count
Invalid/no-auth/visibility requests Rejected Rejected (401, 400, 403, 403) 4 true negatives
Valid public staging Accepted Accepted (200) 1 true positive
Valid queued broadcast Completed without server error Server failure (500) 1 false negative
Invalid request Accepted Not observed 0 false positive

Manual Validation Steps

Set base_url to https://app2-dev.panorra.com. Authenticate as testergothru@gmail.com, save data.token as token, then send the public staging payload above. Finally call GET {{base_url}}/cronjob/broadcast-post. Expected: success without a 500; actual: the type-conversion error shown above. Use only Dev data. The cronjob may process the existing staged queue.

Create a new API for load image from server

QA Summary - 29 July 2026

Result: Passed (developer-confirmed scope).

The image-loader API is reachable and returns the appropriate image bytes for a stored attachment. Developer BE confirmed that this endpoint intentionally supports image attachments only. The allow-list (jpg, jpeg, and png) and rejection of other file types are expected product behavior, not a functional defect.

Endpoint and Test Boundary

GET https://app2-dev.panorra.com/img/attachments/{action}/{file}
  • Environment: Dev.
  • Test data: a disposable Dev image attachment and safe nonexistent/invalid request shapes.
  • Redaction: generated filename, attachment URL, tester identity, authorization data, binary image content, and internal paths are intentionally not included because they are not public-consumption data.
  • No production data or user attachment was used.

Real Dev API Results

Scenario Request shape Observed response Verdict
Existing JPEG attachment GET /img/attachments/b/{safe-file}.jpg 200, Content-Type: image/jpeg, image bytes returned Pass
Missing image attachment Same route with nonexistent safe filename 404 Image not found. Pass
Unsupported action GET /img/attachments/{invalid-action}/{safe-file}.jpg Error JSON: {"status":"error","message":"URL not valid"} Pass: invalid group rejected
Non-image extension GET /img/attachments/b/{safe-file}.txt Error JSON: {"status":"error","message":"File not valid"} Pass: non-image rejected
Traversal-shaped filename Attachment route with encoded traversal-shaped filename File not valid; no image bytes returned Pass: unsafe payload rejected

The successful request confirms that an allowed stored image can be loaded. A nonexistent file does not return image data, and invalid group/file inputs are rejected before an image is sent.

Scope Confirmation

Area Confirmed behavior QA result
Loader purpose Loads supported image attachments from the server. Pass
Attachment content Image files only. Pass
Supported extensions jpg, jpeg, and png. Pass
Missing image Rejected with 404. Pass
Non-image or invalid group Rejected with a safe error body; no image bytes returned. Pass

Source Review

Area Evidence Result
Registered route src/Routes/V1/Routes.go registers GET /img/attachments/:action/:file. Reachable
Attachment groups Only actions b and c are accepted. Guard present
Image allow-list .jpg/.jpeg map to image/jpeg; .png maps to image/png. Correct
Invalid file type Any other extension returns File not valid. Expected rejection
File loading Read failure returns 404 Image not found. Correct missing-file behavior
Successful response Validated content type is set before image bytes are returned. Correct
Path protection Action and extension validation run before file read. Invalid traversal-shaped request did not return file data

Developer Note: HTTP Status Code

For invalid action or unsupported extension, the API currently returns an error body with HTTP 200. The error body correctly prevents unsupported image/file handling. Changing only the HTTP status to 4xx may affect frontend consumers that currently rely on the 200 response and its JSON body.

This status-code alignment is not included in the acceptance scope of this issue. It is deferred pending FE impact assessment and coordinated BE-FE contract work, including validation of the FE error handler/interceptor and every consumer of this endpoint. It does not change the confirmed image-only loader behavior.

If the team chooses to standardize the contract, first verify FE handling for 400 and 404, then release the BE status-code change together with the FE update. This is an improvement item, not a blocker for the requested API.

Test Coverage

Method Coverage Outcome
Black-box Dev existing image, missing image, unsupported action, non-image extension, and traversal-shaped request. Expected image retrieval and rejection behavior confirmed
Gray-box Runtime responses compared with validation and file-read branches. Runtime matches intended image-only scope
White-box Route registration, action/extension guards, content-type mapping, file read, and error branches. Implementation supports confirmed scope

QA Conclusion

The requested API meets the confirmed scope: allowed images load successfully, missing images return 404, and unsupported groups/files do not expose image data. No functional bug is recorded for this issue.

The API for loading Report Bug and Contact Us attachments is reachable and returns the appropriate image bytes for a stored image. Previous Route : {{base_url}}/users/delete-filter

QA Summary - 29 July 2026

Result: Passed. The replacement API deletes the authenticated user's custom filter, rejects a repeat deletion when no filter remains, and rejects unauthenticated requests. No coding defect was observed in the executed Dev scenarios.

Endpoint and Test Boundary

DELETE https://app2-dev.panorra.com/users/delete-filter
Authorization: <tester-token>
  • Environment: Dev.
  • Account: approved tester account only.
  • Test setup: a disposable filter with the public-safe value {} was created through the companion filter-save API, then deleted through the endpoint under test.
  • Cleanup: the disposable filter was deleted successfully. A repeat delete returned not found, confirming no QA filter record remained.
  • Redaction: token, account identifier, generated record ID, and account-specific data are omitted.

Real API Results

Scenario Request Observed response Result
Create disposable test filter POST /users/add-filter, multipart filter_value={} with tester authorization 200; {"statusCode":200,"data":{"valid":true,"messages":"Add Filter Custom Success"}} Setup pass
Delete existing tester filter DELETE /users/delete-filter with tester authorization 200; {"statusCode":200,"data":{"valid":true,"messages":"Delete Filter Custom Success"}} Pass
Repeat delete after cleanup Same authenticated DELETE after successful deletion 409; error body reports Filter Custom Not Found Pass: safe not-found handling
Missing authorization DELETE /users/delete-filter without Authorization 401; {"statusCode":401,"data":{"message":"Unauthorized"}} Pass: authorization required

No HTTP 500 response was observed.

Copyable Public-Safe Request and Response

DELETE https://app2-dev.panorra.com/users/delete-filter
Authorization: <valid-user-token>

Successful response:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Delete Filter Custom Success"
  }
}

After the filter has already been deleted:

{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "valid": false,
    "status": "Forbidden",
    "errors": {
      "message": "Filter Custom Not Found"
    }
  }
}

Source Review

Area Evidence Result
Replacement route src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go registers DELETE /users/delete-filter. Correct
Authentication Global authentication middleware requires Authorization; user identity is read from the verified token. Correct
Role boundary Handler permits only the user role. Correct
Ownership lookup Query selects a filter by the authenticated user_id, not by a caller-supplied ID. Correct
Missing record No record and nil ID both return controlled 409 Filter Custom Not Found. Correct
Deletion Deletes the matched record ID only after ownership lookup succeeds. Correct
Success contract Returns HTTP and body statusCode: 200 with a clear success message. Correct
Internal failure path Database lookup/delete failures map to HTTP 500. Implemented; not observed at runtime

Test Coverage

Method Coverage Outcome
Black-box Real Dev setup, successful delete, repeat delete, and unauthenticated delete. Expected responses confirmed
Gray-box Runtime HTTP/body outcomes compared with authorization, record lookup, and delete branches. Runtime matches implementation
White-box Route registration, role check, authenticated-user lookup, missing-record branch, delete call, and response construction. Implementation supports the requested behavior

Confusion Matrix

Expected classification Observed classification Count
Existing authenticated-user filter deleted 200 success 1
No filter exists for authenticated user 409 controlled not-found response 1
Request has no authorization 401 unauthorized response 1
Unexpected server error Not observed 0

QA Conclusion

The replacement DELETE /users/delete-filter route works against real Dev data: it deletes only the authenticated tester's existing filter, returns a controlled response if no filter exists, and requires authorization. The disposable QA filter was removed during the test. No coding bug is recorded.

Previous Route : {{base_url}}/search/delete-history

QA Summary - 29 July 2026

Content-Type: application/json

  • Account: approved tester account only.
  • Test setup: a disposable search-history entry was created through the companion history API, then deleted using the endpoint under test.
  • Test keyword: a QA-only public-safe marker was used; the exact marker, token, account identifier, and record ID are omitted.
  • Cleanup: deletion succeeded and a repeat request confirmed that the disposable record no longer existed.
  • No production data or pre-existing tester history was intentionally removed.

Real API Results

Scenario Request shape Observed response Result
Create disposable history POST /search/add-history with { "keyword": "<qa-safe-marker>" } and tester authorization 200; Success Add Search History Setup pass
Delete matching history DELETE /search/delete-history with the same keyword and tester authorization 200; Success Clear History Pass
Repeat delete after cleanup Same authenticated delete after successful deletion 400; History Not Found Pass: controlled not-found handling
Missing keyword Authenticated delete with { "clear_all": false } 400; keyword is required Pass: input validation
Missing authorization Delete with a valid public-safe JSON body but no token 401; Unauthorized Pass: authorization required

No HTTP 500 response was observed.

Copyable Public-Safe Payloads and Responses

Delete one history entry:

Area Evidence Result
Replacement route src/Routes/V1/SearchRoutes.go registers DELETE /search/delete-history. Correct

Input contract Body accepts optional keyword and clear_all; a non-clear-all request requires a nonblank keyword. Correct

QA Conclusion

DELETE /search/delete-history works against real Dev data for the safe targeted-delete path: it deletes the authenticated tester's matching history entry, requires a valid request, and does not delete data without authorization. The disposable QA entry was removed. No coding bug is recorded.
